_how: Flavor Trivia (added 16 Nov 2026). One set per date (Nairobi time). Each set: theme, img (photo for the card), qs = 10 questions. Each question: q, a (4 options), c (index of the right option, 0-3), x (one line shown after answering), s (optional story slug for 'Read our story'). Every answer checked against 2+ sources before it goes in. Week: Mon Music, Tue Art & Film, Wed African Brands, Thu Countries, Fri Awards, Sat Sport, Sun History. A day with no set simply hides the Trivia card.

qs.q: Bien, Savara, Chimano and Polycarp made up which Kenyan band?
qs.x: They started as an a cappella trio at Upper Hill School, and guitarist Polycarp joined later.

qs.q: Manu Dibango's 1972 hit "Soul Makossa" came from which country?
qs.x: It started life as a B-side, recorded for Cameroon's hosting of the 1972 Africa Cup of Nations.

qs.q: Which Afrobeat pioneer entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2026?
qs.x: He went in under the Early Influence award. Sade was inducted the same year.

qs.q: Wizkid's "Made in Lagos" came out in which year?
qs.x: It was due on 15 October 2020, but he pushed it to 30 October because of the End SARS protests.

qs.q: The rapper and producer tg.blk is from which Kenyan city?
qs.x: She taught herself to rap and produce in her bedroom, on GarageBand.

qs.q: Which South African singer was known as "Mama Africa"?
qs.x: Born in Johannesburg in 1932, she spent about 30 years in exile for speaking out against apartheid.

qs.q: Burna Boy won his first Grammy with which album?
qs.x: It won Best Global Music Album in 2021, a year after African Giant lost in the same category.

qs.q: Tyla won the first-ever Grammy for Best African Music Performance with which song?
qs.x: It was the category's first year, at the 2024 Grammys, and she beat Burna Boy and Davido to it.

qs.q: "Jerusalema" by Master KG featuring Nomcebo is sung in which language?
qs.x: Burna Boy later jumped on the song for its remix.

qs.q: Diamond Platnumz founded which record label?
qs.x: It's based in Dar es Salaam, and its artists have included Zuchu and Mbosso.

qs.q: Lupita Nyong'o won her Oscar for which film?
qs.x: It was her first feature film role. She won Best Supporting Actress in 2014.

qs.q: Who directed "Rafiki", the first Kenyan feature film at Cannes?
qs.x: Kenya's film board banned it at home just before its 2018 Cannes premiere.

qs.q: FESPACO, Africa's biggest and oldest film festival, is held in which city?
qs.x: It started in 1969 and runs every two years in Burkina Faso's capital.

qs.q: In Thandiwe Muriu's photo series "Camo", the women…
a: Blend into a background of the same fabric
qs.x: She's a self-taught Nairobi photographer who picked up a camera at 14.

qs.q: Who directed the Kenyan film "Supa Modo"?
qs.x: It premiered at the 2018 Berlin film festival and was Kenya's Oscar entry that year.

qs.q: Ghanaian sculptor El Anatsui makes his famous shimmering tapestries out of…
qs.x: He flattens liquor-bottle caps and stitches them together with copper wire.

qs.q: Ousmane Sembène, called the "father of African cinema", was from which country?
qs.x: He was a novelist first, and turned to film so more people could reach his stories.

qs.q: Which South African film won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film in 2006?
qs.x: It was the first South African film ever to win an Oscar.

qs.q: What was Netflix's first African original series?
qs.x: The South African spy thriller, starring Pearl Thusi, premiered in February 2020.

qs.q: Nollywood is the film industry of which country?
qs.x: By number of films made, it's the second-biggest film industry in the world, after India's.

qs.q: Safaricom launched M-Pesa in which year?
qs.x: It went live on 6 March 2007. "Pesa" is Swahili for money.

qs.q: Tusker beer is named after…
a: The elephant that killed co-founder George Hurst
qs.x: Hurst died on an elephant hunt in 1923, and his brother Charles named the beer in his memory.

qs.q: Bata, the shoe brand many people assume is Kenyan, was founded in which present-day country?
qs.x: The Baťa siblings started it in Zlín in 1894.

qs.q: The very first Nando's opened in 1987 in which city?
qs.x: It started in Rosettenville, a Johannesburg suburb, and was named after co-founder Fernando Duarte's son.

qs.q: What does MTN stand for?
qs.x: The Johannesburg-based network started out in the 90s as M-Cell.

qs.q: Which airline calls itself "The Pride of Africa"?
qs.x: KQ started using the line after its public share offer in 1996.

qs.q: Amarula cream liqueur is made from the fruit of which tree?
qs.x: Elephants love marula fruit too, which is why there's one on the bottle.

qs.q: In 2019, which became the first African tech startup to list on the New York Stock Exchange?
qs.x: It began trading as JMIA on 12 April 2019, while staff in Lagos rang a bell at the same moment.

qs.q: Tecno, one of Africa's best-selling phone brands, is owned by a company from which country?
qs.x: Its parent, Transsion, is based in Shenzhen and also owns Infinix and itel.

qs.q: Africa's biggest cement producer belongs to which billionaire?
qs.x: Dangote Cement runs in 10 African countries. Rabiu's BUA is a big rival.

qs.q: Which African country has the most people?
qs.x: Over 230 million people at the last count, the biggest population on the continent by a long way.

qs.q: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
qs.x: Dar is still the biggest city and business hub, but parliament moved to Dodoma in 1996.

qs.q: Which is Africa's biggest country by land area?
qs.x: About 2.38 million km², most of it Sahara. DR Congo is a close second.

qs.q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
qs.x: Lesotho is an enclave, a whole country sitting inside another one.

qs.q: Africa's newest country became independent in 2011. Which one?
qs.x: It split from Sudan on 9 July 2011 after a referendum where nearly 99% voted to leave.

qs.q: South Africa has how many capital cities?
qs.x: Pretoria runs the government, Cape Town has parliament, and Bloemfontein has the courts.

qs.q: Which country grows the most cocoa in the world?
qs.x: It has led world production since the late 1970s, well ahead of neighbouring Ghana.

qs.q: Which country's flag has an AK-47 on it?
qs.x: It's the only national flag in the world with a modern rifle, crossed with a hoe on an open book.

qs.q: Which country is known as the "Land of a Thousand Hills"?
qs.x: In French it's "Pays des Mille Collines".

qs.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in which country?
qs.x: It sits right by the Kenyan border, but the whole mountain is in Tanzania. It stands 5,895 m tall.

qs.q: Burna Boy won his first Grammy for which album?
qs.x: It won Best Global Music Album in 2021, a year after African Giant lost to Angélique Kidjo.

qs.q: Wizkid got his first Grammy for his part on which song?
qs.x: Beyoncé's "Brown Skin Girl" won Best Music Video in 2021, the same night Burna won his first.

qs.q: Tems won her first Grammy for which song?
qs.x: The Future and Drake song samples her track "Higher". It won Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023.

qs.q: Who won the very first Grammy for Best African Music Performance, in 2024?
qs.x: "Water" beat Burna Boy, Davido, Asake, Olamide and Ayra Starr in the category's first year.

qs.q: South Africa's Black Coffee won a Grammy in 2022 in which category?
qs.x: He won for "Subconsciously", his first nomination and first win.

qs.q: Who is the only African player ever to win the Ballon d'Or?
qs.x: He won it in 1995, the first year non-Europeans could be voted for. He later became Liberia's president.

qs.q: Who was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize?
qs.x: The Kenyan environmentalist won it in 2004 for her work on sustainable development, democracy and peace.

qs.q: Who was the first Black African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
qs.x: The Nigerian playwright won it in 1986.

qs.q: Abdulrazak Gurnah, the 2021 Nobel Literature winner, was born on which island?
qs.x: He left Zanzibar at 18 after the 1964 revolution and became a writer and professor in England.

qs.q: Five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo is from which country?
qs.x: She was born in 1960, when the country was still called Dahomey.

qs.q: Eliud Kipchoge ran the first marathon under two hours in which city?
qs.x: He ran 1:59:40 on 12 October 2019. It doesn't count as a world record because of the special pacing.

qs.q: Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome running…
qs.x: He was the first Black African to win Olympic gold, and he won again in Tokyo four years later.

qs.q: Which was the first African team to reach a men's World Cup semi-final?
qs.x: They beat Portugal 1-0 in the 2022 quarter-final in Qatar.

qs.q: Which country has won the most Africa Cup of Nations titles?
qs.x: Seven titles, the last in 2010. Cameroon are next with five.

qs.q: David Rudisha set his 1:40.91 800m world record at which Olympics?
qs.x: He led from start to finish and became the first man to run 800m under 1:41.

qs.q: Kenya's men's rugby sevens team is nicknamed…
qs.x: Shujaa is Swahili for courage or heroism.

qs.q: Faith Kipyegon has won three Olympic golds in which event?
qs.x: Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, the first athlete to win three Olympic 1500m titles.

qs.q: Which three countries will co-host AFCON 2027?
qs.x: The Pamoja bid won in September 2023. It's the first time any of the three will host.

qs.q: What is the nickname of Kenya's national football team?
qs.x: It comes from harambee, the Kenyan tradition of pulling together for a common cause.

qs.q: Before the 2022 semi-final, which African teams had reached a World Cup quarter-final?
qs.x: Cameroon in 1990, Senegal in 2002 and Ghana in 2010 all went out at that stage.

qs.q: On what date did Kenya become independent?
qs.x: June 1963 was self-rule (Madaraka). Kenya became a republic exactly a year after independence, in 1964.

qs.q: In 1957, which became the first sub-Saharan African country to win independence?
qs.x: Kwame Nkrumah led the Gold Coast to independence on 6 March 1957 and renamed it Ghana.

qs.q: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 prison years on which island?
qs.x: The island sits off Cape Town. He walked free in 1990.

qs.q: At the Battle of Adwa in 1896, Ethiopia defeated which European army?
qs.x: Emperor Menelik II's victory on 1 March 1896 kept Ethiopia independent.

qs.q: The Organisation of African Unity was founded in 1963 in which city?
qs.x: 32 countries signed its charter on 25 May 1963, which is why 25 May is Africa Day.

qs.q: Mansa Musa, famous for his gold-filled trip to Mecca in 1324, ruled which empire?
qs.x: He handed out so much gold passing through Cairo that people talked about it for generations.

qs.q: Zimbabwe takes its name from…
qs.x: Great Zimbabwe, the stone city near Masvingo. The name is usually traced to the Shona for "houses of stone".

qs.q: Which Kenyan town is called the oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement in East Africa?
qs.x: Lamu Old Town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.

qs.q: The railway from Mombasa to Lake Victoria got which nickname?
qs.x: Critics in Britain called it a lunatic line because of its cost and the lives lost building it.

qs.q: Which Mau Mau leader has a statue on Kimathi Street in Nairobi?
qs.x: He was hanged at Kamiti Prison on 18 February 1957. The statue went up 50 years later, in 2007.
